reason: Every part of the r10 claim is now false for the reason 98e195a9 gives (tests exist). enforce_bodyless (mcp-re-http-profile/src/mcp_transport/mod.rs:121-129) is reached via verify_bodyless_request (bodyless/mod.rs:385) and pinned by tests/bodyless_202_test.rs:688-747 (unsupported -> McpProtocolVersionUnsupported, supported -> Ok, default policy also refuses), so an Ok(()) body goes red. The absent-header design choice is pinned too: sign_bodyless_request adds no MCP-Protocol-Version (no such string in bodyless/mod.rs), and bodyless_202_test.rs:405-454 verify Ok under VerifierPolicy::default() (:60-62), whose profile_default policy has require_protocol_version_header=true (mcp_transport/mod.rs:79,96-98). Tests live in the integration file rather than the module, which does not matter for the claim.

Same as 019c7acc: tests/bodyless_202_test.rs:688-747 drives enforce_bodyless end-to-end through verify_bodyless_request (bodyless/mod.rs:385) under strict and default policies; deleting the check turns :714-718 and :742-746 red. 98e195a9 is false for the same reason (the function has an executable witness).

The r10 facts still hold as design (active_snapshot clones out, custody/mod.rs:379-381; retirement does not reach held handles), but r10 itself made the verdict depend on whether the hot-path signer re-reads after an epoch advance, and that is what 5c9a19db answered: DelegatedServerSigner::current re-reads per exchange and serves only nbf<=now<exp (mcp-re-proxy/src/delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:245-254); advance publishes the successor or retires on Err (:346-364); the bound is documented at :231-244. The delegated key is pub(crate) (custody/active_key.rs:149) so signing needs a SigningWindow, which opens none at/after exp (custody/signing_window.rs:52-61, control :155-158). A declined advance keeping the predecessor until exp is the design recorded as positive control 9e009b28. Same reason as the false-positive.

Only the production-risk half is inside accepted-risk 82a62fe9, and for the same reason: the single production factory is the OS CSPRNG (mcp-re-proxy/src/delegated_wiring.rs:173). The row's main claim is an overstated guarantee: the fleet-uniqueness claim is presented as test-backed when the test sets up the very property it asserts. That claim is still present at e01172e0. The test is still named and documented for fleet uniqueness (custody/mod.rs:624-633) and is still handed factory_seeded(10)/(200). The comment still says delegated_kid 'carries the fleet-wide uniqueness' (:427-428). The default factory() still starts at n=100 on every construction (:491-497). There is no producer-side distinctness test in delegated_wiring.rs (its tests at :265-413 never compare two delegated_kids). 82a62fe9's own adjudication calls this part a claim-only defect with work_class CLAIM_CORRECTION, and that work has not been done. A risk acceptance about the factory does not make an overclaiming test name true.

Add a distinctness test at the producer (mcp-re-proxy/src/delegated_wiring.rs mod tests). reason: Both retire sites build the event through retired(&a, now) (custody/mod.rs:215-226), which carries a.jti()/a.nbf()/a.exp(): in reissue at :208-211 and in hold_off at :333-336. jti is read from the credential into ActiveDelegatedKey (active_key.rs:137, 166-168). There is no String::new() or nbf: 0 left in the file. Control at :653-669 asserts that retired jti/nbf/exp equal the issued ones. Every part of the r10 claim (empty jti at both sites, fabricated nbf 0 / exp now) is covered by ce02cfd4's fix.

CustodyConfig carries window: DelegatedKeyWindow (custody/mod.rs:108-110). Its fields are private (key_window.rs:71-74) and its only constructor refuses overlap<=0 and overlap>=ttl (:81-89), so ttl>0 also follows. rotation_due and mintable read window.overlap()/ttl() (mod.rs:234, 278), and an unrepresentable now+ttl fails before the root is touched (issuance_terms.rs:52-56). Both r10 failure modes (per-call root and born-expired) are unconstructible. d1fde0dd's fix covers them.

body_protocol_versions yields the version from BOTH top-level _meta and params._meta (mcp_transport/mod.rs:135-146), and check_protocol_version refuses if any of them differs from the covered header (agreement.rs:102-109). That also forces the two limbs to agree with each other, which covers the inverse case r10 raised. The exact split-body case is controlled at mod.rs:334 and the params-only case at :316. 80939a7b's fix covers every part.

reissue returns Result<Option<..>>, with Ok(None) when the root declined and the predecessor is retained (custody/mod.rs:194-213). advance_trust_epoch maps Ok(None) to TrustEpochAdvance::Declined (mcp-re-proxy/src/delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:352-359). apply_epoch_advance leaves last_label unmoved on Declined and retries (signing_plane/trust_epoch_advance.rs:120-148). issue_now clears the hold-off so the commanded attempt is real (custody/mod.rs:246-249). 0e8ca83c's fix covers both the silent Ok and the no-retry consequence.

An executable witness now exists. the_minted_credential_carries_the_configured_scope_and_trust_epoch verifies the minted credential and asserts that verified.delegated_key equals the snapshot's key (custody/mod.rs:975-1000). On top of that, ActiveDelegatedKey::issued refuses a credential whose cnf key is not the held key (active_key.rs:92-94). That check catches a build() that writes a wrong x, because it compares against the held key rather than against the request. Witnessed by a_credential_attesting_another_key_fails_the_issuance_closed (mod.rs:526-553).

The divergence is gone: no owner reads emptiness as 'no contract' any more. The proxy classifier carries the set verbatim (mcp-re-proxy/src/config_state/mcp_transport_contract.rs:36-40) and violations refuses an empty or blank set (:43-57, control :79-83). serving_capabilities always builds mcp_2026_07_28 (serving_capabilities.rs:134-146). The policy type's reading of empty is deny-all (mcp_transport/mod.rs:73-104; agreement.rs:90-101), which matches the module's 'The contract is mandatory' (mod.rs:28-30), and there is no 'Unconstrained' anywhere in the transport code. Empty-to-deny-all is the single, fail-closed reading and is recorded as positive control c0f61e26. Minor: classify is total over empty input, so 'a held state names a version' depends on violations running first, but even then it would fail closed rather than diverge.

Same as a67c3fb7. Layer A no longer has an Unconstrained classification (config_state/mcp_transport_contract.rs:20-57 refuses empty as a configuration error), so the 'opposite classifications on either side of the seam' claim no longer holds. The public type still admits an empty set, but it reads it the same fail-closed way as every other owner (positive control c0f61e26).

r10 deferred the verdict to whether the hot-path signer re-checks exp per request, and it does: current() serves only nbf<=now<exp (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:245-254). Signing needs a SigningWindow, which opens none at/after exp (signing_window.rs:52-61). The key is pub(crate) (active_key.rs:149). Test half: post-exp use is controlled by snapshot_fails_closed_past_expiry (dss/mod.rs:539), issuance_failure_serves_the_valid_key_then_fails_closed_at_expiry (:560) and an_expired_credential_opens_no_window (signing_window.rs:155-158). Retirement is observable through the shared cell (fail_closed_issuance_retires_the_snapshot, :548). By design it is not observable through an already-held handle (documented at :231-244). Same reason as 5c9a19db.

issue_if still compares only exp (custody/mod.rs:268), but the future-nbf scenario r10 names can no longer be adopted. issued refuses claims.nbf > requested nbf, and the requested nbf is the issuance now (active_key.rs:124-130; build sets nbf=now at mod.rs:415). The hot path also checks nbf (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:251, control :754). The first-pass residue is accurate and minor: custody's own sign_response with a caller now earlier than a prior issuance (a non-monotonic clock) skips nbf.

Both divergence errors map to McpReError::MalformedEnvelope (error/core_projection.rs:64-66), and wire_code() projects through that mapping (core_projection.rs:162-164). The mcp-re.malformed_envelope code is asserted for McpMethodDivergence (tests/mcp_transport_headers_test.rs:215-216, 261-262). First-pass residue is accurate: no test asserts McpTransportDivergence's wire code directly.
